title: SafeImpute: Reliable Clinical Data Imputation via Conformal Selection

problem.claim: Sparse patient visits and irregular test ordering create pervasive missingness in key clinical laboratory indicators.

gap.claim: Existing imputation methods provide limited guidance about which imputed values are reliable enough for high-stakes downstream use.

contributions.claim: SafeImpute is a reliable imputation framework for irregular and sparse clinical longitudinal records.
SafeImpute combines an event graph, a two-relation GNN with adaptive fusion, and an auxiliary masked reconstruction objective to learn imputations.
SafeImpute uses conformal p-values and the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure to control the false discovery rate of clinically unacceptable errors among released imputations at a user-specified tolerance.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on Mayo Clinic data and the public MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV datasets report strong imputation accuracy and reliable error control.
The authors report that SafeImpute outperforms diverse baselines in standard imputation evaluation and FDR-controlled selective-release evaluation.
Code is reported as available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Clinical longitudinal data contain pervasive missingness because visits are sparse and tests are ordered irregularly.
Accuracy-focused imputation methods offer limited reliability guidance for high-stakes use.
The work aims to produce accurate imputations while selectively releasing reliable results with statistical control over clinically unacceptable errors.
SafeImpute models clinical records with an event graph and learns imputations using a two-relation GNN, adaptive fusion, and masked reconstruction regularization.
Conformal p-values and Benjamini-Hochberg control are used for selective release, and experiments report accuracy and error-control results across three datasets.

source_observation.claim: Selective release can pair imputation with an explicit procedure for controlling unacceptable errors among released values.

interpretation.claim: For high-stakes missing-data workflows, reliability-aware selection may be more actionable than optimizing average imputation accuracy alone.

application.claim: A downstream system could expose only imputations passing a user-specified error-control tolerance.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish performance or applicability beyond the reported clinical datasets and evaluations.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset sizes, missingness patterns, evaluation metrics, baseline identities, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the conformal calibration procedure or assumptions required for its guarantees.
The abstract does not establish clinical deployment outcomes or independent verification.
